knowledge.title: SPEC04 — Typed ordered preferences
knowledge.text:
SPEC04 — Typed ordered preferences
Components:
MM02, MM04, RE01, RE02, UX03
Behavioral contract:
Closed keys are preferred_response_language={en,hi} and preferred_response_format={concise,detailed}. All user changes, including panel writes, receive customer sequence from accepted_user_events. Per key/scope atomic conditional UPSERT accepts only a larger source sequence. Panel expected_version is checked before successful acceptance. Include first-write serialization, unique event keys and DELETE tombstones. Pending overlay follows source order and applicable scope; persisted status requires committed projection.
Failure/recovery contract:
Invalid provenance/key/value -> reject; stale source -> ignored_stale; stale panel version ->409; extraction failure -> failed/retry status and remove only that pending overlay.
Acceptance criteria:
Force older English after newer Hindi, concurrent first inserts, duplicate jobs, DELETE before old SET, competing panel/chat events and failed extraction. Verify projection, output language, version/order and truthful UI state.
Excluded:
Arbitrary inferred profile fields in typed preferences; worker-completion order as user order; temporary instructions as automatic global updates.

knowledge.title: SPEC06 — Correction, forgetting and retention
knowledge.text:
SPEC06 — Correction, forgetting and retention
Components:
MM04, SP05, AU03
Behavioral contract:
Block deleted source material and dependent serving paths before acknowledging active erasure. Track direct memory, preference payloads/source spans, vectors, summaries, cache, checkpoints, accepted jobs and restore plans. Preserve minimal ordering tokens without forgotten content. Physical cleanup has separate store-specific status. Assign retention purpose/owner and explicit limits for local and external stores.
Failure/recovery contract:
Any required serving invalidation fails -> deletion remains pending/incomplete. Do not claim provider/backups/public copies deleted based on a local tombstone.
Acceptance criteria:
Seed direct/derived canaries, delete during backlog and query exact/paraphrase/old value across stores. Stale work cannot resurrect value; separate restore-and-scrub drill proves declared backup handling.
Excluded:
Legal compliance claims or a fixed legal retention schedule; real customer content in published artifacts.

knowledge.title: SPEC13 — Resettable world and scenario harness
knowledge.text:
SPEC13 — Resettable world and scenario harness
Components:
BD04, EV01, PL01
Behavioral contract:
Dedicated synthetic schema/DB and Redis/file namespace per trial. Pin fixture/tool/policy/source versions; script state changes. DomainClock is separate from security expiry and monotonic budgets. Reset canonical semantic state and verify no contamination. Initial runner calls the same API/service wiring as the demo; deterministic stubs are labeled.
Failure/recovery contract:
Non-test reset target -> refuse. Mismatched initial state -> invalid trial; insufficient setup -> blocked, not a passing benchmark.
Acceptance criteria:
Two clean resets match canonical hashes; parallel trials share no mutable state; state changes reproduce by script; regular application role cannot reset fixtures; frozen banking date cannot freeze session expiry.
Excluded:
Real customer records, assuming fixed fixtures make model output deterministic, or shortcuts that bypass production authorization.

knowledge.title: SPEC01 — Authentication and browser session
knowledge.text:
SPEC01 — Authentication and browser session
Components: SP01, UX02, PL03
Behavioral contract: Use configured OIDC code flow with PKCE S256 and vetted callback/token validation. Map issuer/subject to internal customer. Redis stores opaque rotated sessions; __Host-bank_sid is Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, without Domain. All mutation routes check CSRF token and allowed Origin. Deployed banking profile disables legacy unauthenticated chat. Session expiry is checked at API entry and before queued banking access; logout clears browser working state.
Failure/recovery contract: Invalid or expired identity -> 401; invalid CSRF/origin -> 403; required auth store unavailable -> access closed, 503. Never select customer from a request field.
Acceptance criteria: Good login accesses only owned resources. Invalid issuer/audience/signature/state/nonce, callback replay, old session after rotation/logout, and cross-site mutation are rejected. Test long SSE expiry and queued access after logout.
Excluded: Building an identity provider, storing passwords, or unsigned development authentication in deployed banking profiles.

knowledge.title: SPEC02 — Authorization, resource identity and database roles
knowledge.text:
SPEC02 — Authorization, resource identity and database roles
Components: SP02, SP03, BD01, PL01
Behavioral contract: Principal is server-created and carried in RequestContext. Gateway and domain/provider service authorize each resource. Display masks resolve within owned lists and ambiguity produces authorized choices. Runtime roles are nonowner, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS with no privileged role membership. RLS uses trusted transaction-local customer context and write checks; composite owner FKs prevent mismatched children. Restrict dispatcher, worker and migrator separately.
Failure/recovery contract: Missing or foreign resource -> non-enumerating 404; missing tenant context -> deny. Unknown operation/schema -> typed reject before provider access.
Acceptance criteria: Exercise API, direct provider, worker and real pooled DB paths with two customers. Valid owner succeeds; foreign UUID, missing context, stale pooled context, spoofed headers/body, arbitrary SQL/tool names do not expose evidence or execute a write.
Excluded: Guaranteeing isolation after complete application/DB-credential compromise; customer masks as canonical IDs; broad admin sessions in request handlers.

knowledge.title: SPEC12 — Audit, telemetry, privacy and runtime configuration
knowledge.text:
SPEC12 — Audit, telemetry, privacy and runtime configuration
Components: AU01, AU02, AU03, OB01, OB02, OB03, SP05, PL03
Behavioral contract: Action success audit shares local support transaction and runtime cannot edit/delete it. Redacted JSON logs and OTel linked spans use metadata allowlists; no raw bank facts/secrets/prompts by default. Metrics use bounded route/tool/status labels, no customer/request IDs. Propagate trace IDs across outbox as correlation only. Validate issuer/secrets/environment at startup; separate liveness from dependency readiness. Govern synthetic eval traces separately.
Failure/recovery contract: Mandatory audit failure rolls back support; optional exporter failure drops/buffers bounded telemetry with diagnostic counter. Unknown price -> cost unavailable. Missing auth config/store closes banking access.
Acceptance criteria: Synthetic secret canaries never export in tested sinks; forged trace cannot authorize; spans link across process hop; queue/dead-letter alerts exercised; bad environment fails safely; runtime audit update/delete denied.
Excluded: Tamper-proof audit against DBA compromise, uptime inferred from CI YAML, or raw sensitive labels/content everywhere for convenience.

knowledge.title: SPEC11 — Durable workers, deduplication and recovery
knowledge.text:
SPEC11 — Durable workers, deduplication and recovery
Components: RE01, RE02, RE03, RE04, AO01, AU02

Behavioral contract: Transactional outbox is acceptance source. Dispatcher claims bounded batches with short transaction and lease generation. Consumer claims unique handler receipt as same-tx gate before local effect. A fencing generation serializes reclaim and checkpoint/terminal-event publication so replaced workers cannot publish. Retry only classified transient errors within budgets; unsupported schemas/permanent failures dead-letter visibly. Durable local operation lookup resolves unknown outcomes.

Failure/recovery contract: Lost acknowledgment replays receipt; lease expiry alone is not success. Duplicate read/model computation may occur and is measured; duplicate logical effects/public terminal answers must not.

Acceptance criteria: Crash before/after effect commit, deliver twice, pause A until B reclaims/completes then resume A, and exhaust retry/dead-letter paths. Capture remains durable and stale ownership cannot publish.

Excluded: Transport exactly-once guarantee, unbounded retries or automatic archival replay beyond the supported retention/version window.

knowledge.title: SPEC05 — Working context and long-term semantic context
knowledge.text:
SPEC05 — Working context and long-term semantic context
Components: MM01, MM03, AO03, UX01

Behavioral contract: Working state holds bounded recent context and authorized canonical selections scoped by customer/session/conversation/version. Precedence: explicit current-response instruction, active conversation preference, global preference, default English/concise. Separate optional semantic history from exact settings and bank/policy truth. Retrieve only governed permitted source/derivative records; summaries retain lineage.

Failure/recovery contract: Ambiguous selection -> clarify; session changes clear transient selections/proposals. Optional memory failure degrades personalization explicitly when relevant; it never supplies a missing current bank fact.

Acceptance criteria: Follow-up resolves correct authorized product; multiple matches clarify; another session cannot consume a pending proposal; temporary Hindi does not overwrite global English; historical balance cannot override current tool evidence.

Excluded: Unbounded prompt history, cross-session pending proposal reuse, implicit global memory for every utterance.

knowledge.title: SPEC03 — Durable turn API and response transport
knowledge.text:
SPEC03 — Durable turn API and response transport
Components:
 UX01, UX02, AO01, RE01
Behavioral contract:
 POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/turns validates ownership and input then atomically persists accepted_user_event, turn/run and outbox before 202. customer/client_turn_id uniqueness provides replay. Same client key with a changed normalized request returns 409. GET status is recovery authority; persisted per-run event IDs support SSE reconnect. Emit answer.ready only after completed-answer checks. Disconnect does not cancel accepted work. Persist a canonical request fingerprint on turn acceptance so idempotency compares the same normalized operation fields, rather than only client_turn_id.
Failure/recovery contract:
 No durable commit -> no successful acceptance. Unknown commit -> reconcile by original client identity. 401/404/409/422/429/503 retain safe request IDs. Client merges repeated events by event ID.
Acceptance criteria:
 Duplicate and concurrent same-key requests return one logical turn; changed input conflicts. Restart/disconnect after acceptance and reconnect from last event recovers authorized ordered state without duplicate rendering.
Excluded:
 Financial token streaming before validation; treating SSE itself as durable or exactly-once transport.

knowledge.title: SPEC07 — Typed banking enquiry services
knowledge.text:
SPEC07 — Typed banking enquiry services
Components:
 BD01, BD02, BD04, UX01, SP03
Behavioral contract:
 Synthetic accounts expose current/available balance distinctly; cards distinguish daily limit, credit limit, available credit and outstanding; transactions have explicit status/date and deterministic cursor order; existing loans expose principal/APR/payment; EMI schedule and actual payments are separate evidence. UUID refs, source version/as_of, currency and integer-string minor units are mandatory. Pin supported currency exponent metadata; enforce ranges, Decimal APR and no mixed-currency sum.
Failure/recovery contract:
 Unknown decline/payment reason remains unknown. Unsupported currency/range -> typed failure. Bank timeout -> unavailable; no stale memory fallback. Resource changes require fresh reads.
Acceptance criteria:
 Compare service DTO and rendered answer to DB oracle for debit/credit, declined/pending/posted/reversed, timestamp ties, all pages, multiple cards, null reason, scheduled-unpaid EMI and large/zero amounts. Supported exponent formatting remains exact.
Excluded:
 Money movement, live bank connections, new loan decisions, limit increases, card-setting changes, travel notices and formal refund/dispute execution.

knowledge.title: SPEC09 — Bounded planning and answer construction
knowledge.text:
SPEC09 — Bounded planning and answer construction
Components:
 AO01, AO02, AO03, AO04, SP03, RE04
Behavioral contract:
 One coordinator uses registered enquiry tools and support drafting. Strict tool/plan schema rejects extras and model-created identity. Structured provider errors distinguish unavailable, invalid and no evidence. Typed bank facts are server-rendered; optional explanatory prose is checked and falls back to supported templates/limitations. Trace included sources and usage. All repairs/retries count against common call and monotonic deadline budgets. Persist logical run start/deadline and atomically reserve model/tool attempts against durable counters before dispatch. Reclaim/restart does not reset call/deadline allowance. Derive process-local monotonic remaining budgets from the real execution deadline, never from fixture DomainClock; duplicate in-flight calls may still consume real cost and must be reported.
Failure/recovery contract:
 Unknown capability -> explain unsupported; invalid plan -> at most one bounded repair then clarify/error; insufficient mandatory context -> narrow rather than drop decisive evidence. No loop continues beyond budget.
Acceptance criteria:
 Inject malformed JSON, unknown tools, SQL-like args, merchant/policy injection, wrong numeric draft, unsupported citations, provider emptiness/timeouts and evidence-position perturbations. No invented bank field or consequential execution is shown.
Excluded:
 Model-triggered support execution, multi-agent supervisor by default, private chain-of-thought as an eval requirement.

knowledge.title: SPEC08 — Policy ingestion, applicability and explanation
knowledge.summary: SPEC08 — Policy ingestion, applicability and explanation Components: KR01, KR02, KR03, AO03 Behavioral contract: Immutable versioned synthetic policy documents/chunks carry product/scope/locale/source hash and half-open UTC effective interval. Activate complete sets atomically. Distinguish current versus historical applicability. Exclude ineligible evidence on every serving path. Start exact eligible-vector plus lexical search; measure hybrid before ANN/reranker changes. Record lane degradation. Citations resolve to known version/section, and explanations require claim support rather than reference membership alone. Failure/recovery contract: Missing/conflicting applicable rule or unsupported prose -> limitation, clarification or support. Partial retrieval is allowed only when surviving evidence independently supports the material answer. Acceptance criteria: Test future/expired/overlap/timezone boundary, wrong-product near duplicates, embedding/lexical lane failure, relevant-but-nonentailing citation and incomplete ingestion. Relevance and answer support get separate measurements. Excluded: Open-web policy fallback, automatically adding CRAG/Self-RAG/reranking agents, or treating a citation as proof of correctness.
